title: Signal-fusion rollback controller for canary / A/B rollouts
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Summary:
We need a robust, low-noise automated rollback controller that fuses multiple SLO signals (latency, error rate, token cost, throughput) for canary and A/B rollouts. Current single-metric triggers produce false positives during bursty traffic and when cost/throughput tradeoffs shift. This ticket defines the design and implementation plan for a signal-fusion controller that: performs cohort-aware comparisons, applies statistical tests instead of raw thresholds, adapts thresholds by load and baseline variance, and exposes tunables for rapid on-call adjustments.

Goals:
- Avoid noisy rollbacks while keeping a tight guardrail on severe regressions (latency p99, 5xx rate).
- Make cost (per-token spend) an explicit rollback dimension so we can discontinue costly model variants automatically when they materially increase unit cost without improving quality/latency.
- Support staged responses: partial traffic evacuation, throttled canary halt, immediate full rollback for catastrophic signals.
- Provide observability and manual override for SRE/PM/Eng.

Non-goals:
- Replace human judgement for nuanced quality regressions (semantic quality must still go through eval gates).
- Solve every edge-case cohort correlation (we will start with user-agent, region, and route cohorts).

Design overview (high level):
1) Signal inputs: per-minute windows for p50/p90/p99 latency, request error rate (4xx/5xx split), token-cost-per-request, and throughput (rps). Each datapoint is tagged with cohort dimensions (route, region, customer_tier).
2) Baselines: maintain rolling baseline distributions for each metric per-cohort (default lookback 1 week, configurable). Compute both median and variance, expose EWMA smoothing for short-term noise control.
3) Detection ensemble: three detectors run in parallel for each release vs baseline:
   - Relative uplift detector: computes percent change vs baseline with variance-normalized z-score.
   - Sequential hypothesis test: SPRT for error rate and change-point detection for latency (fast detection, low false positive rate).
   - Bayesian posterior check: estimates probability that new variant is worse than baseline by a practical delta (e.g., >10% p99 latency or >2x 5xx).
4) Fusion logic: produce a composite severity score (0-100) by weighted combination of detectors with per-signal weights. Weights depend on SLO priority (e.g., p99 latency weight high for latency-critical routes, token cost weight higher for batch embed jobs).
5) Action tiers:
   - Tier 0 (inform): composite_score in [20, 40) — create dashboard annotation and a low-severity alert to #canary-monitoring.
   - Tier 1 (throttle): score in [40, 70) — pause ramping; freeze canary traffic at current allocation and run extended observation period (default +10m).
   - Tier 2 (evacuate partial): score in [70, 90) — drain a configurable fraction of traffic (e.g., 50%) back to baseline and add the release to a cooldown set.
   - Tier 3 (rollback): score >= 90 OR catastrophic single-metric breach (5xx > 5% absolute) — immediate full rollback with incident stub created.
6) Safety checks: require detection in at least two independent cohorts OR consecutively across two windows (window length default 1m) before Tier2/3 actions to avoid flapping. We also require a minimum sample size during low traffic to avoid noisy triggers.
7) Cost-aware decisioning: token-cost delta contributes positively to severity only when quality/latency do not improve. If new model is cheaper but slightly slower within SLO, do not rollback; conversely, if cost increases > X% and quality unchanged, escalate to Tier1/Tier2.

Tuning and adaptive thresholds:
- We will implement an automatic threshold tuner that adjusts composite score weightings and detection sensitivity by tracking historical false positive/negative outcomes (supervised signal refinement). The tuner runs offline weekly, suggesting hyperparameter adjustments which are gated by human review.
- For high-variance routes (e.g., search endpoints), the controller increases observation window (EWMA alpha reduced) and requires more confirmation windows.

Observability / telemetry:
- New rollout-controller metrics: composite_score, detector_signals (raw zscore, sprt_result, bayes_prob), action_taken, confirm_count, cohort_keys.
- Dashboard: rollouts -> {release} -> safety timeline with signal overlays and decisions. Alert rules mapped to Tier1+ with runbook links.
- Tracing: add rollout.id and cohort tags to request spans to attribute incidents quickly.

Implementation plan (tasks):
- Add controller service module (rollout-controller) in infra/rollouts. Creates API: evaluate(release_id, window).
- Instrument metrics pipeline: update metrics-collector to emit per-release cohort windows.
- Implement detectors: relative_uplift, sprt_error_detector, bayesian_delta_detector.
- Implement fusion and action executor with feature flag gating (ff: signal_fusion_rollbacks).
- Add simulation harness & unit/integration tests with synthetic traffic patterns.
- Create dashboards and SLO alerting for Tier 1+ actions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller runs behind FF and can be toggled per-org.
- Simulations show false positive rate < 1% on synthetic bursty traffic while detecting 95% of regressions > practical delta within 5 minutes.
- Rollout dashboards visualize every decision step and raw signals.
- On-call runbook and emergency abort endpoint exist.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-automation causing customer-impacting rollbacks. Mitigation: gradual opt-in by org, default conservative thresholds, require multi-cohort confirmation for high-impact actions.
- Risk: Metric delayedness causing stale decisions. Mitigation: prefer short windows for fast signals and require sample size; add leader election for controller to avoid duplicate actions.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Signal+Fusion+Rollback+Controller
- Simulation harness PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/1423
- Initial dashboard queries: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/rollouts/signal-fusion
- Related Linear tickets: ENG-41234, ENG-35820

Implementation notes for engineers:
- Use existing metrics pipeline (kafka -> metrics-aggregator) and add a release_id tag at aggregator stage to avoid sampling bias.
- Implement detectors as independent modules with uniform Detector interface so new algorithms can be swapped without changing fusion logic.
- Persist decisions and raw inputs to the rollouts audit table (S3/Parquet) for retrospective tuning and ML-based tuner input.

Post-launch plan:
- 2-week canary: enable for internal orgs only; gather precision/recall stats; tune weights.
- Month 1: enable for early enterprise customers behind opt-in.
- Month 2: allow global enabling for lower-priority routes with conservative defaults.
